tool_applicability_notes: DifferenceWitness/common abstraction: both source and target problems can have a locally valid or structurally stronger surrogate while the root-critical bridge is missing; HM1a's root-critical coordinate is an actual Chow source plus exact assembly/equality, not continuum normalization.
DifferenceWitness/material change: HM1a has no lattice-spacing limit or transfer-matrix gap. The tool is reused only as a logical bridge-audit operation, never as Yang-Mills mathematics.

Applicability preconditions pass for proposed decomposition routes because the surrogate (graded/filtered/categorical condition), root object (alpha in Hdg^p(X)), bridge map (cycle/correspondence plus assembly), and preservation property (surjective source realization of alpha) can all be stated explicitly.

Cheapest regression: reject any route whose remaining graded-piece surjectivity, representability, or support assumption is exactly the unsolved cycle-map surjectivity for that piece; retain only reductions that discharge pieces by proved source constructions or independently proved Hodge-vanishing.
failure_reuse_notes: F-XM001 is a transfer warning only: a successful surrogate certificate need not preserve the root-critical coordinate through an additional bridge.
The Yang-Mills adversarial sequence is not imported into Hodge theory; only the diagnosed bridge-omission pattern is used.
A Hodge-specific failure record should be created only after a concrete HM1a route fails its source/assembly audit.
unresolved_warnings: Arapura's Leray criterion is an exact theorem, but applying it to arbitrary X may leave a graded cycle-map surjectivity obligation as hard as the root.
Arapura's universal-sheaf correspondence mechanism is special-case geometry, not a general constructor.
Abstract motivation or categorical realization may still substitute a larger source category for Chow.
H4d1 can propagate an existing witness but cannot supply initial algebraicity.
